subject: Weekend rapid-routing carveout request — APAC migration window
messages:
From: Anil Rao <anil.rao@breezefin.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekend rapid-routing carveout request — APAC migration window

Vanessa,

We're planning a database migration for BreezeFin's APAC edge (SFO->SIN failover) on the weekend of Oct 18-19. Expected traffic surge + transient latency spikes between 02:00-06:00 SGT. To avoid noisy P1s going through the standard global escalation flow (which could add ~20-30m handoffs), we'd like to request a temporary routing carveout for high-severity incidents:

- Duration: 48 hours starting 2025-10-18 00:00 SGT
- Behavior: Route P1s from APAC origin to the BreezeFin-dedicated hot seat (on-call @breezefin-ops) with an expedited ladder (engineer -> ops lead -> Redwood on-call) for the window.
- Justification: Minimize duplicate paging and reduce mean time to acknowledge while the migration stabilizes.

Can Redwood enable a short-term routing policy and an exception to the P1/P2 inbox routing for that window? We're happy to accept a carveout with telemetry obligations and a documented rollback.

Attachments: [Attachment: breezefin-migration-runbook.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)]

Thanks,
Anil Rao
Head of Platform
BreezeFin
anil.rao@breezefin.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anil Rao <anil.rao@breezefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekend rapid-routing carveout request — APAC migration window

Anil — thanks for the heads up and the runbook.

Apple-to-oranges summary of what we can do quickly:

- We can provision a temporary routing rule that forwards APAC-origin P1s to a dedicated escalation target (hot seat) for a bounded window.
- We'll need:
  1) A signed mutual action plan (MAP) that defines rollback triggers and telemetry thresholds.
  2) Clear oncall handoff details for the hot seat (name, phone, escalation contact).
  3) A short telemetry stream (3 key traces/latency dashboards) to confirm degraded behavior vs. outage.

Operational ask: our standard approval for exception windows is that an SRE lead (Redwood) and the customer's ops lead are both reachable on the hot-seat. Ben — can you confirm capacity for a hot-seat from Redwood for 36–48h? Marissa — can you own the MAP template and the routing policy ILS?

We'll treat this as an escalation-related exception and will only enable the carveout after MAP and runbook approvals. If useful, I can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to iron details.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub referenced: breezefin-migration-runbook.pdf]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anil Rao <anil.rao@breezefin.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekend rapid-routing carveout request — APAC migration window

Vanessa / Marissa — I can staff a Redwood hot-seat for the migration window but recommend we tighten the duration to 36 hours (start 2025-10-18 00:00 SGT -> 2025-10-19 12:00 SGT) to limit blast radius.

Operational points:
- Hot-seat staffing: Ben (primary), backup (SRE: Jonah), and a paging rotation to kick in at midnight SGT.
- Escalation ladder: 0-5m engineer ack -> 10m ops lead -> 30m Redwood SRE.
- SLA credit: per D-8421, credits only apply if service-level degradation exceeds 180 consecutive minutes; we should document thresholds in the MAP.

Links:
- Rollout plan (internal): https://app.redwood.com/rollouts/D-8421
- Draft MAP (placeholder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/runbook-placeholder

Anil — please confirm the hot-seat contact details and whether BreezeFin will accept the 36h window and the escalation ladder above.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Engineer
Redwood Inference
